text:
Egor Chinakhov has the hardest shot in our tracking this season, a 98.9 mph blast that ranks at the very top of the league, and he's one of its fastest skaters too. What he doesn't have yet in Pittsburgh is the production: three goals and five points in 14 games, at 15 minutes a night.

His own numbers are fine. He's shooting right at league average and his chances are about where you'd expect, 0.81 expected goals per 60. The issue is what happens around him. The Penguins have a five-on-five expected-goals share 4.8 points lower with him on the ice than without him, and last season Evolving-Hockey had him drawing tough competition, 91st percentile.

He came from Columbus, where he was a first-round pick in 2020, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked how he attacks: carrying the puck in on most entries and getting to the slot. Our range has him around 20 goals and 41 points. A spot on the top power play, where the shot would do the most damage, is what we'd watch for.
headline: Egor Chinakhov has the shot and needs the role
